notes.title: Hotfix to previous update
notes.content: [p]Includes the fix to "IT LOOKS A BIT LIKE A DOG, DUNNIT?" that removes an unintended shortcut, and turned off the no-use-to-anyone-else developmernt mode that sends you to a black screen after two seconds of the title screen. Sigh.[/p]

notes.title: Don't Go Breaking (out of) My Heart
notes.content: Fixed a bug where it was possible to stray outside the bounds of one of the levels.

notes.title: Update: Multiple Save Slots!
notes.content:
By sort-of-popular request, Gemima now offers three save slots so you can try out the different modes without losing progress.

The previous main menu items of "Continue Game (mode)" and "Start New Game" have been replaced with a single "Play" menu item which takes you to the new save slot screen. Here you can start or continue games in three separate slots, each with an inventory panel so you can quickly see your progress.

Enjoy!

notes.title: Handle With More Care
notes.content: Removed an unintended shortcut from one of the puzzles.

notes.title: Quick Thinker Update
notes.content:
New saves started in "Quick Thinker" mode now have a six hour overall completion timer rather than individual puzzle timers.

This timer is pitched as a challenge to new players who think they're fast at solving puzzles, not a speed run target (which would be much lower). Enjoy!

notes.title: The End Really Is The End Now
notes.content: Fixed a bug where you would be left with one irritatingly un-ticked door after viewing the credits.

notes.title: Minor Update: Spelinng Misstakes, timely achievement awards, long-lasting titles
notes.content:
Fixed a couple of small spelling mistakes and missing spaces.

Achievements should now unlock as you achieve them rather than at the end of your play session

Level titles remain present for a little longer to allow you to read them.

notes.title: Update: Fix for "Landslide" being rather easier than intended!
Tweaks And Features!
notes.content:
Couple of quality of life changes in this update:

1. The invisible 'player ghost' that stays behind to stop rocks falling instantly when you move now hangs around a little longer

Old version: 233ms when moving laterally, 33ms when moving down
New version: 233ms when moving laterally, [b]166ms[/b] when moving down

This makes certain manoeuvres involving both players a little less finnicky.

2. [b]Slow mo![/b]

To make it easier to execute certain moves involving rocks and gems, I've also added the option to enable and disable [b]Slow-Mo[/b] at any time from the pause menu. This halves the movement speed of Gemima, Jules, and everything else in the game.

However, it does [i]not[/i] slow down the level timer if you are playing with one enabled, so use these new powers judiciously...

notes.title: Update: Fix for people with awkward monitor aspects, like my wife.
notes.content: The puzzle "8 BIT SOFTWARE IS SUPERIOR" should now look less janky on 16:10 monitors.

notes.title: Update 7 : Reorganisation!
notes.content:
After much soul-searching I decided that some of the puzzles required for completion on the main spine of the game would be better placed elsewhere. This shouldn't adversely affect anyone's progress, but let me know if I'm wrong!

Also added some missing entries to the end credits.

notes.title: Minor Update 5: My Wife Keeps Finding Shortcuts
notes.content: This time it's BRIDGEWORK that she's managed to short-circuit. But not any more!

notes.title: Minor Update 5: Fixed a too-easy puzzle
notes.content: My long-suffering wife found a sneaky too-easy solution to CRATE NORTH ROAD that has now been been ruthlessly expunged. Count yourself lucky if you sneaked through the same way...

notes.title: Minor Update 4: Added some thanks to the credits!
notes.content: Wanted to thank the people who have helped playtest and provide feedback!

notes.title: Minor Update 3: Added another teachy-puzzle
notes.content: DIAMONDS IN THE ROUGH is another puzzle you encounter before being explicitly forced to use the necessary tools. No more!

notes.title: Minor Update: Fix for requiring a game technique before it has been introduced.
notes.content: Some levels got shuffled around during the design process, and I've realised that one puzzle required a technique that had not yet been introduced. This update tweaks the affected puzzle so that it can be completed without that technique, but doesn't otherwise meaningfully affect the puzzle.

notes.title: Minor Update: Bug fixes + extra flavour text
notes.content: A tiny update to fix text not respawning correctly after an undo, and to add a little more chat between Gemima and Jules.
